Welcome
It is a pleasure to welcome you to Forest Park School. We are a Hampshire local authority maintained special school. We provide education for children and young people aged 2-19 years with severe, profound and complex learning difficulties. In addition, the majority of our pupils have co-existing conditions such as Autism, Down Syndrome and physical disabilities.
Our mission statement at Forest Park is ‘opening the door to what’s possible’ and through this we are dedicated to providing a highly personalised curriculum and stimulating learning environment, which starts with the individual needs of each child and young person and takes them on a journey of personal success.
In addition, we are committed to ensuring that our pupils enjoy school, are happy, confident and proud of themselves and their achievements. Through our five core values of ‘independence’, ‘communication’, ‘aspiration’, ‘resilience’ and ‘respect’ we seek to prepare every member of our school community for the next significant phase in their life.
I hope you enjoy finding out more about our school through the website and look forward to welcoming you to our wonderful school at some point in the future.

pageCache.text:
Post-16 Courses and Accreditation
As students move into the Post-16 phase of their education, their strengths and interests are key to creating a highly personalised and bespoke curriculum pathway. The curriculum and courses on offer are developed in line with students complex and wide-ranging needs. In addition, the curriculum at Post-16 aims to provide young people with opportunities to learn essential skills that prepare them for their future adult life.The curriculum offers students the opportunity to gain accreditation through ASDAN Personal Progress. These qualifications are designed to address the needs of our pupils and ensure that all learners are given the equal opportunities to access appropriate and relevant course content to develop new skills and prepare them for future adult placements. Pupils study ASDAN Personal Progress units throughout their three years within Post 16 and will leave us with a recognised qualification working at Entry 1 level. These units are selected in line with pupil interest and needs to support application and generalisation of functional life skills. Our SEEDS pathway is designed for our more sensory based and complex learners. Our Roots and Shoots pathway has been designed for our more practical based learners showing some independence within their functional skills.
Please click the link below for an overview of the ASDAN Personal Progress units studied

pageCache.text:
PE & Sport Premium
Primary PE and Sport Premium
We want all of our children to be fit, active and lead healthy lives. As such, alongside our formal PE lessons we promote physical activity in a range of different ways, appropriate to pupils’ needs throughout the day.
All pupils at Forest Park have at least two hours of PE lessons each week. This will typically take the form of one PE lesson and one swimming lesson. Where pupils are unable to go swimming, they will typically have an outdoor PE lesson involving more adventurous activity or bike, trike and scooter riding.
In addition, pupils have regular timetabled slots on the trampoline, swings, bikes and scooters.Physiotherapy programmes including walking and standing form an integral part of physical development for some pupils.Pupils really enjoy the summer term sports days which encourage healthy competition and team work through a variety of inclusive and accessible sporting events.

Personal Development
At Forest park School we recognise that pupil wellbeing is a priority and focus on individual’s personal development in all aspects of school life. Our aim is to develop happy pupils who have a strong sense of self and are able to communicate this to others. We place great value on providing strategies to enable our pupils to regulate their emotions and be ready to learn.
Personal Development covers a wider range of core areas:
Pupil’s Personal Development learning is woven through everything that we do at Forest Park School and we utilise every opportunity to support the development of our pupils. We believe that learning reaches far beyond the classroom! All pupils have personal key skill targets that link with at least one of the core areas, as well as their EHCP outcomes. Staff ensure opportunities to practise and develop these skills are planned into each individual’s week as appropriate to them.
Personal Development is also taught weekly through specific PSHE lessons where pupils focus on different areas:
Lessons are practical, fun and multi-sensory to ensure pupil’s can apply key concepts learnt to their everyday lives.
We also plan and deliver special day and week events that link to our Personal Development curriculum area such as ‘Friendship week’ and ‘Pride week’. This gives our pupils opportunities to celebrate the diverse world we live in and recognise their own and other’s personal achievements and contribution.

Governors
The Governing Board at Forest Park School supports and challenges school leaders to ensure that the school fulfils its statutory responsibilities and delivers the best possible outcomes for every pupil. This includes oversight of safeguarding, finance, special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), equality, compliance, staffing and educational performance.
The Governing Board is responsible for setting the school's vision, ethos and strategic direction. Governors provide strategic leadership, scrutiny and accountability, ensuring that decisions are made in the best interests of pupils and that public funds are used effectively. The Headteacher is responsible for the day-to-day operational management of the school and for implementing the strategic priorities agreed by the Governing Board.
As school governors we focus on six key questions:
Our aim is to work with the Headteacher and senior leadership team to drive strategic development and raise standards for all the pupils and young adults at Forest Park School.
Chair of Governors
Paul Shields - appointed September 2023
Email: paul.shields@fpshants.co.uk
Before becoming a governor, I spent 15 years in the travel industry, working in product management and procurement for specialist long-haul tour operators. I later established my own consultancy, providing sales and marketing support to luxury hotels and tourism businesses around the world.
Outside work and governance, I am a keen road cyclist and have taken part in a number of races in France, as well as charity rides in Spain, France, South Africa and Namibia. I am also a lifelong rugby supporter and have enjoyed coaching youth rugby. More recently, I can usually be found on the touchline watching my son's matches and wishing I was still young enough to join in!

Sue Thomas - appointed March 2024
From 2017, I served as the Designated Clinical Officer for Special Educational Needs and Disabilities across several health boards—a role I thoroughly enjoyed. In 2017, I earned an MSc in Integrated Governance for Health and Social Care from the University of Westminster. I retired from nursing in 2024 where my career spanned the NHS, social care, and independent and international healthcare.
I moved to West Wellow in 2018. As I approached retirement, I wanted to give back to the community, particularly in the field of Special Educational Needs, which led me to apply to become a school governor.
Forest Park School is a remarkable place where every pupil is recognised as an individual and supported to develop their skills and learning at their own pace. The school always feels welcoming and positive.

Jo Pizzo - appointed September 2023
I have been a proud member of the Forest Park team since 2016, when I first joined the school as a Learning Support Assistant and in 2019 I began my teacher training here. Since qualifying, I have continued my journey at the school as the teacher of Cherry Class on the Secondary site.
I specialise in working with pupils with profound and multiple learning disabilities (PMLD) and am passionate about supporting pupils to develop their communication and independence, to enable them to express themselves and make choices.
Alongside my classroom role, I am a member of the school’s Personal Development curriculum team and am the whole-school lead for Relationships and Sex Education (RSE), reflecting my strong interest in supporting pupils’ wider personal development and helping them build the skills, understanding and confidence they need as they grow towards adulthood.
I became Staff Governor in 2023 and really value the opportunity this gives me to contribute to the continued development of Forest Park beyond my own classroom, sharing my experiences to help inform Governing Body discussions and decisions.

Maths
At Forest Park School we believe that teaching and practising key maths concepts helps our learners to make sense of the world around them and problem solve. We present maths as a functional skill and ensure that using and applying is threaded throughout all areas of our maths curriculum. Our pupils are presented with purposeful, individualised learning that is practised in a range of contexts meaningful to them.
Each child receives an individualised Maths pathway that focuses on their current achievement and their next steps. Maths is taught daily through pupil’s individual key skills, as well as small group learning opportunities. We make maths practical and fun and provide opportunities for pupils to generalise their knowledge. We place a strong emphasis on developing pupil’s understanding of number to equip them with skills they can apply in their everyday lives.
We also ensure our pupils are presented with a broad range of learning areas within maths through our topic work - this includes:
We believe learning Maths concepts doesn’t just happen in the classroom. We continue to weave learning opportunities throughout our school day in all areas to make it meaningful and relevant to each individual pupil.

School Uniform
At Forest Park School we value our school uniform as a symbol of belonging to our school community. We hope that pupils feel a sense of pride and belonging to their school. We also recognise that for many pupils, their school uniform acts as an ‘object of reference’, indicating the difference between a school day and a home day.
It is our policy that all pupils from Nursery to Year 11, wear school uniform when attending school. However, we understand the differing needs of our pupils and believe that it is extremely important that pupils feel comfortable in school and wear clothes that support their sensory and physical needs, along with their own well-being.
All uniform should be in the colours listed below. It should be plain and not contain logos / branding or any other colours. It is not necessary for uniform to be embroidered with the school logo and as such items in the appropriate colours can be purchased from a wide range of retailers.
For families who would like uniform with the embroidered school logo on it, a range of items including sweatshirts, cardigans, polo shirts and PE kit are available to purchase through Skoolkit in Totton: https://www.skoolkit.co.uk/
Please ensure all uniform, kit and shoes are permanently labelled with pupil name

About Us
Forest Park School is a Hampshire local authority maintained special school. We provide education for children and young people aged 2-19 years with severe, profound and complex learning difficulties. In addition, the majority of our pupils have co-existing conditions such as Autism, Down Syndrome and physical disabilities.
Forest Park is split across two sites, one mile apart. The Primary School is a purpose-built special school in Ringwood Road Totton and caters for around 100 pupils. The Secondary School is in Commercial Road Totton, catering for around 40 young people with the most profound and complex learning difficulties.
The school has a dedicated team of teaching and support staff with a wide range of experience and expertise in teaching and supporting pupils with severe and complex learning difficulties.
In school we are supported by and work in collaboration with a range of professionals including School Nurses, Speech and Language Therapists, Physiotherapists and Occupational Therapists.
At Forest Park we create a positive environment for learning through a culture of high expectation, supported by our mission statement of ‘opening the door to what’s possible’. Through our core values of ‘communication’, ‘independence’, ‘aspiration’, ‘resilience’ and ‘respect’ we support and develop our children and young people to excel in all areas of their development and be ready for the next significant phase in their life.
The school’s ambition is to create a child centred, personalised approach to learning that begins with each child and young persons individual needs. Through a creative, practical and fun learning environment we aim to offer a meaningful and relevant curriculum tailored to individual need.
Pupils at Forest Park enjoy school and contribute positively to the whole school community. They are encouraged to be independent at every opportunity, confident and show pride and enjoyment in their learning and that of others.

Creativity
At Forest Park School we promote and encourage freedom of expression from all of our pupils. We believe that creativity allows our pupils to express themselves as individuals and allows many to excel away from the need of cognitive and logical thinking. Creativity allows our pupils to be imaginative and playful in a safe, non-judgemental environment.
We feel it is vital to offer our pupils a broad and balanced curriculum and value the wider opportunities the creative arts provides. Research tells us that being creative supports our positive wellbeing and acts as a mood enhancer.
Our core areas of Creativity include:
We view the process of creativity as the fundamental element where our pupils learn and place less emphasis on the final product. We encourage experimentation, playfulness and fun when our pupils tackle the different core areas of creativity. Our pupils learn the skills of creativity when experimenting with different media and demonstrate their individuality through the choices they make during the creative process.
Creativity is woven throughout our curriculum and is often the focus of delivery within many of the other curriculum areas. This is achieved through opportunities to play, experiment with pattern and shapes, songs and rhymes, expressive communication, Attention Autism sessions and role play, to name a few.
Each year our children take part in a focused ‘Arts Week’ where they collaborate with their peers to produce multiple pieces of art, focused around a particular topic or theme. Our pupils thrive and take great pleasure in showcasing their creations at the end of the week in the Gallery, that is shared with their families and friends.
